items.title: Brent rises 3.3% to $95.82 as Iran diplomatic hopes fade despite bearish EIA inventories
items.summary: Brent finished November 12 near $95.82, up 3.3%, and WTI was reported at $88.74, up 2.6%, after President Trump said the United States did not need an Iran deal. The rally overwhelmed a 4.7-million-barrel U.S. crude inventory build. This confirms a market risk-premium repricing, not a newly verified shipping closure.

observations.label: November 12 benchmark close, Brent
observations.value: $95.82 a barrel, +3.3%, independently reported by Associated Press and Wall Street Journal

observations.label: November 12 WTI reported by Wall Street Journal
observations.value: $88.74, +2.6%; second independent closing-price confirmation not obtained for WTI

observations.label: EIA November 12
observations.value: Commercial crude stocks +4.7 million barrels to 414.4 million; inventories roughly 4% below five-year seasonal norm

observations.label: Physical-flow differentiation
observations.value: Previously documented Hormuz tanker attacks persist; no new closing of a route, stoppage of exports or vessel strike independently verified in this pass. MARAD regional advisories 2026-011 and 2026-013 remain active

observations.label: Watch / invalidation
observations.value: UKMTO and MARAD notices, actual vessel transits, Gulf exports, tanker freight, IEA monthly report November 13, Brent-WTI spread and XLE/XOP strength. Credible diplomatic progress would reduce the premium

items.key_finding: Diplomatic-risk repricing outweighed bearish inventories at the oil close, without new proof of reduced physical flows.

sources.title: Associated Press, U.S. markets and oil November 12
Wall Street Journal, November 12 oil reversal

items.title: Global Payments falls sharply as CD&R and GTCR abandon take-private talks
items.summary: Global Payments fell roughly 9% to 11% in November 12 trading after Reuters reported that CD&R and GTCR dropped early takeover talks. Sources cited the complexity of arranging financing for a major leveraged transaction. The lost buyout catalyst adds pressure to the payments company, but the business remains operating and another bidder or renewed discussions cannot be ruled out.

observations.label: Share reaction, November 12 afternoon
observations.value: Barron's reported around -10.7% near $90.90; Reuters report appeared about 12:12 PM ET. Intraday indication, not independently confirmed closing quote

observations.label: Catalyst
observations.value: Reuters, citing two people familiar, said CD&R and GTCR withdrew from early-stage acquisition discussions

observations.label: Fundamental interpretation
observations.value: Take-private financing appears difficult at current debt costs; this does not establish deterioration in Global Payments merchant-processing volumes

observations.label: Watch / invalidation
observations.value: Company statement, revised M&A interest, leverage/credit costs, payment volume growth and merchant margins; a new credible bidder would counter the lost catalyst

items.key_finding: A financing-constrained take-private withdrawal removed a major potential catalyst for GPN.

sources.title: Reuters exclusive, CD&R and GTCR drop pursuit of Global Payments, November 12
Barron's, Global Payments declines after reported buyout talks withdrawal

items.title: Super Micro slumps on reported DOJ export-control scrutiny tied to Megaspeed
items.summary: Super Micro shares dropped about 9% to 12% on November 12 as Bloomberg and Semafor reported federal inquiries concerning possible diversion of AI servers to China. Super Micro says it has cooperated with authorities, and the Justice Department has not publicly confirmed a new charge against the company. Strong AI-server demand does not remove compliance, concentration and margin risks.

observations.label: Share reaction, November 12 regular trading
observations.value: Barron's reported SMCI down about 9.2%; other intraday reports showed declines of 10%-12%. Not independently confirmed closing figures

observations.label: Investigative status
observations.value: Bloomberg reported DOJ inquiry into links between Megaspeed-related entities and alleged China server diversions; Semafor separately reported inquiries citing administration officials. Allegations are not findings of guilt

observations.label: Company position
observations.value: Super Micro says it cooperated with US and Taiwan authorities, that Megaspeed never was its customer, and an internal review found no current senior-management knowledge of an alleged scheme

observations.label: Fundamental assessment
observations.value: Demand for AI servers remains strong, but export-control risk, customer concentration and low-margin hardware assembly can complicate growth

observations.label: Watch / invalidation
observations.value: Official DOJ statements or filings, export-control rule changes, customer orders, product shipments, cash flow and gross margin; formal clearance would reduce legal uncertainty

items.key_finding: Fresh independently reported probe allegations raise AI-server execution and compliance risk, but have not been adjudicated.

sources.title: Barron's, Super Micro falls on reported DOJ probe, November 12
Semafor report covered by Investing.com, November 12
Financial Times, Singapore's Megaspeed investigation, November 12

items.title: Nvidia pares 14% intraday fall to about 5.4% as AMD and Broadcom advance
items.summary: Nvidia declined about 5.4% at the November 12 close after sliding as much as 14% following its CEO transition. AMD and Broadcom gained roughly 4% to 5% while Nvidia-linked CoreWeave remained weak. The split suggests selective repricing of leadership, supplier and financing exposure rather than proof of collapsing AI infrastructure demand.

observations.label: Nvidia close, November 12
observations.value: AP and ChartMill independently reported about -5.4%; intraday low was roughly -14%

observations.label: Competitor and customer moves
observations.value: Late-session ChartMill: AMD around +4.7%, AVGO around +5.1%; Barron's reported CoreWeave down about 6.8% intraday. Exact closes not independently confirmed for all

observations.label: Broad-market close
observations.value: AP reported S&P 500 roughly -0.3% to -0.4%, Dow -0.4%, Nasdaq -0.4%; small-caps were weaker

observations.label: Fundamentals / risks
observations.value: AI accelerator demand remains supported, but Nvidia succession, potential export-policy shifts and CoreWeave credit/customer concentration create differentiated risks

observations.label: Watch / invalidation
observations.value: NVDA succession, November 17 earnings, hyperscaler orders, official export policy, CoreWeave financing and semiconductor breadth; broad-based chip weakness would undermine the selective-rotation interpretation

items.key_finding: The session closed with Nvidia-specific selling but competitor strength, distinguishing company risk from general AI-demand weakness.

sources.title: Associated Press, closing market recap November 12

items.title: Soft U.S. 30-year Treasury auction underscores long-term financing risk
items.summary: The November 12 U.S. Treasury 30-year auction attracted weaker demand than October's sale despite a lower high yield. Its bid-to-cover fell to 2.36 from 2.54 and the sale tailed the when-issued yield by 0.4 basis point. The result adds to borrowing-cost scrutiny for capital-intensive AI infrastructure and housing, but one auction cannot establish a sustained funding squeeze.

observations.label: U.S. Treasury auction, November 12 approximately 1:00-1:50 PM ET
observations.value: $25 billion new 30-year bonds priced at 5.441% high yield; when-issued 5.437%, a 0.4 basis-point tail

observations.label: Demand versus October
observations.value: Bid-to-cover 2.36 versus 2.54 prior and about 2.44 recent average; indirect bidder share about 68% versus 72% in October

observations.label: Price qualification
observations.value: High yield was lower than October's 5.618% despite softer bidding; do not infer rates rose solely because of the auction

observations.label: Concurrent rates and oil, November 12 afternoon
observations.value: AP reported the 10-year Treasury yield near 5.10% versus 4.98% Tuesday and Brent around $95.82 (+3.3%) intraday, amid uncertainty around Iran diplomacy; these are changing observations, not settlements

observations.label: Watch/invalidation
observations.value: Treasury secondary yields and auction-demand follow-through, inflation and oil risk, corporate credit spreads, data-center project financing, housing mortgage rates; stronger future auctions or easing yields would temper the signal

items.key_finding: Softer long-bond demand is a timely funding-cost warning, not proof of a systemic credit problem.
